web_evidence.title: The Day of the Jackal — Penguin Books sample
web_evidence.note: Penguin's authorized sample supplies a sustained Chapter One excerpt narrated externally across Bastien-Thiry, de Gaulle, the OAS conspirators, and Rodin, including characters' perceptions and beliefs without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: The Day of the Jackal by Frederick Forsyth (1971) | Books & Boots
web_evidence.note: The whole-book review describes the narrative as splitting between the Jackal's preparations and Lebel's investigation and supplies page-identified interior passages externally narrating multiple characters, corroborating a nonparticipating narrator throughout the novel.

search_log: Searched "The Day of the Jackal" "Frederick Forsyth" excerpt and opened Penguin's authorized 40-page sample.

Searched "The Day of the Jackal" with "third person," "third-person omniscient," "point of view," "narrator," and "narration"; explicit claims found mainly on Reddit or low-quality pages were not used.
Searched for narrative-technique and literary-analysis sources; the Cambridge crime-fiction result mentioned the novel but did not identify its narrative person.

Searched Google Books, Open Library, Internet Archive, and Penguin domains; Google Books supplied catalog and publisher-description pages but no accessible diagnostic interior excerpt, while no useful Open Library or Internet Archive result surfaced.
Opened the Guardian's author-annotated feature; Forsyth discussed the novel's technology and plot but not its narrative person, so it was not used as person evidence.
Opened the contemporary Kirkus review; it was plot synopsis rather than explicit POV evidence and was not used.
Opened the Books & Boots whole-book review and used its structural description and page-identified interior passages as corroborating evidence.
Unofficial full-text and audiobook-transcript mirrors surfaced in search but were excluded in favor of the authorized Penguin excerpt.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person. The strongest Goodreads passages move externally among the Jackal, Rodin, and other characters, including knowledge unavailable to a focal character; none exposes a narratorial I or sustained you. Penguin's authorized opening independently sustains this external narration, and the whole-book review corroborates the same structure across the Jackal and Lebel plot streams. The only limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers the opening rather than the entire novel, but the interior Goodreads evidence and page-spanning review evidence resolve that scope limitation, with no indication of alternating base narration.
